name: Ladakh Vernacular Trombe Wall Shelter
description: A traditional high-thermal-mass vernacular structure featuring 450mm sun-dried adobe brick walls paired with a double-glazed south-facing Trombe wall for passive solar collection.
key_features: 450mm thick adobe sun-dried earth block wall (high thermal mass)
South-facing glazed solar thermal collector aperture
Traditional mud-straw insulated ceiling with poplar wood rafters
Naturally stabilized internal temperature swing

name: Tibetan High-Mass Stone Mountain Refuge
location_suitability: Zanskar Range, Hemis High Valleys (>4,000m ASL)
description: A rugged Himalayan shelter built from thick granitic stone blocks backed with an inner mineral wool insulating cavity and solid deodar timber roof structure.
key_features: 500mm dressed mountain stone masonry for extreme thermal inertia
Inner mineral wool cavity preventing thermal bridging
Recessed south triple-glazed windows with nighttime insulated shutters
Massive heat retention for remote off-grid resilience
expected_performance: Damps sub-zero swings; continuous steady indoor temperature.

name: High-Altitude Military Defense Pod
location_suitability: Siachen Glacier, Kargil Ridge, Daulat Beg Oldi (>4,800m ASL)
description: An ultra-insulated, rapidly deployable composite shelter designed for extreme arctic sub-zero winds (-35°C) and sub-atmospheric pressure.
key_features: Multi-layered composite wall with 100mm high-density EPS core
Airtight envelope with controlled mechanical heat-recovery ventilation
Triple-glazed argon-filled south solar apertures (U = 0.9 W/m²K)
Minimal envelope thermal bridging and rapid thermal responsiveness
expected_performance: Ultra-low heat loss rate (<350W total) in -30°C conditions.

name: Geodesic Cold-Arid Arctic-Style Dome
location_suitability: Pangong Tso Basin, High Passes (>4,300m ASL)
description: An aerodynamic geodesic timber dome maximizing internal volume while minimizing external heat-radiating surface area. Optimized for fierce mountain winds.
key_features: Aerodynamic icosahedral geometry minimizing convective wind chill
Lightweight timber struts with dense Sheep Wool & EPS triangular panels
Overhead zenith south-angled solar collector skylights
Central thermal mass rock-bed storage
expected_performance: High solar harvesting efficiency and minimal wind deflection loss.

name: Spiti Super-Insulated Earthbag Cabin
description: An earthbag-tube constructed sustainable retreat with a curved mass envelope, sheep-wool sub-floor insulation, and an attached direct-gain sunspace.
key_features: Curved thermal mass envelope reducing wind turbulence and surface exposure
Local renewable sheep-wool thermal blanket insulation (50mm)
Low embodied energy utilizing on-site mineral earth and clay
Integrated greenhouse thermal buffer
expected_performance: High thermal stability with 75%+ hours in comfort band.

name: Ladakh Passive Solar Greenhouse Habitat
description: Combines a southern glazed solar greenhouse for cold-climate food production and thermal buffering with a heavily insulated rear residential core.
key_features: Southern greenhouse buffer zone acting as a dynamic solar pre-heater
Rear rammed-earth Trombe wall with operable air vents for convective circulation
High daytime heat gain transferred into deep stone flooring
Dual benefit of fresh food security and zero-emission heating
expected_performance: Peak daytime temperatures up to 25°C; nighttime buffer > 15°C.
